messages:
Ava (support): quick heads-up — Acme saw a ~15–25s window of 429s during a short spike even though their account shows a cushion enabled. customer says traffic was ~120 rps for ~30s and then back to normal. pasted failing response headers below:

Ava (support): ```HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 10:32:12 GMT
X-RateLimit-Limit: 60000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 161
X-Burst-Cushion-Remaining: 0
X-Burst-Cushion-Refill-Rate: 0.5
Content-Type: application/json
```

Ava (support): customer also shared this quick curl that hit the 429s when run with concurrency 40: ```for i in $(seq 1 200); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***' -d '{"prompt":"x"}' & done; wait```

Jamal (eng): thanks — a few quick checks: can you grab their per-minute and per-second token usage metrics around 10:32? also want to see any backend error spikes. my hunch: either the smoothing window + fractional refill produced a temporary accounting gap, or concurrent requests raced to consume remaining fractional credits.

Priya (product): product note: the cushion refills as a fractional rate (credits/sec) but we persist in whole-units in some places for efficiency. that can create a brief visible dip under high parallelism. also verify whether background backfills (batch jobs) used the same account that minute.

incidents-bot: ALERT: quota-drain detected for account acme-app at 2026-03-10T10:32:09Z — abrupt drop of 98% of cushion within 18s. Relevant team: support, eng.

Luis (support): @Ava can you provide the org id and the exact minute-level metrics (tokens_in, tokens_out, concurrent_requests) from the console? we need to correlate.

Ava (support): org: acme-app-42 — I pulled minute buckets: 10:31 => 11k tokens, 10:32 => 75k tokens, 10:33 => 9k tokens. concurrent requests peaked ~125 during 10:32. no scheduled batch jobs listed but customer had a background reindex job that kicked at 10:31:55 (they say it was short).

Jamal (eng): that pattern fits an accounting race: many requests read cushion value simultaneously, each assumes credits available and decrements locally before central writeback. with fractional refill rounding you can hit zero while in-flight requests still succeed briefly then get 429s once central store updates. I'll grep logs for sync failures and add additional instrumentation.

Priya (product): immediate mitigations we can suggest to customer: throttle concurrency on client side (e.g., max parallel 24), enable smoothing window to 60s (increases effective cushion smoothing), or temporarily raise their tier burst_limit for the next hour while we investigate.

Luis (support): can you give a concrete repro script we can ask the customer to run in a dev workspace so we can reproduce from their network?

Ava (support): repro script I sent to customer (they ran it and reproduced):
```bash
#!/bin/bash
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %time_total\n" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"prompt":"short"}' &
done
wait
```
run with CONCURRENCY=40 via xargs -P to simulate the same parallelism. they saw 20–30 429s clustered in the 30s window.

Jamal (eng): thanks — I'll instrument the atomic update path and add a short-lived mutex around cushion decrement for the hot path to avoid double-read races. small perf cost, but worth it as a patch. also adding finer telemetry: per-request pre-check vs post-write result so we can see the race in production traces.

Priya (product): I'll open a config task to expose a per-org smoothing override in the console so SRE/support can raise smoothing quickly for customers in-flight. also tracking a follow-up to adjust how we persist fractional credits to reduce rounding shocks.

Ava (support): sent the customer a workaround: reduce client concurrency to 24 and enabled a one-hour smoothing bump — they confirmed reduced 429s on a follow-up test. they'll leave the temporary changes for us to monitor.

Luis (support): please ping here once Jamal has the instrumentation PR so we can coordinate a customer-facing postmortem and suggested best practices doc.

Jamal (eng): PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/7881 — adds atomic cushion decrement + telemetry tags. will roll canary tonight.

Priya (product): I'll draft a short KB: "Why short spikes can cause temporary 429s even with cushion enabled" and include suggested client settings.

Ava (support): perfect — I'll keep the customer updated and close when canary + KB live. thanks team :thumbsup:
